<subject>NAAG Engagement</subject>
<body>
Dear Team,

I have finally connected with Anjali Sharma, our contact at the National Association of State Advocates ("NASA") regarding their role on telecom matters, particularly concerning Section 271 approvals.

Anjali informed me that there is no formal group effort in place (i.e., no telecom committee or a designated advocate leading telecom issues). Individual state advocates may get involved on a case-by-case basis. For instance, the Maharashtra State Advocate, Rajesh Kulkarni, recently opposed Reliance Communications' application for 271 approval, but the regulatory authority still granted Reliance’s petition.

Anjali suggests we leverage the state advocates as much as possible. For example, if we have evidence showing a lack of local competition, we should share this with the relevant state advocate and ask them to represent our interests. Anjali acknowledges that Agriculture India Pvt. Ltd. supports competitive markets, and typically the state advocates would align with our stance — so this is something to keep in mind moving forward. While there is no certainty that the regulator will heed the advocates, it could be a worthwhile approach.

Please share any thoughts or feedback you may have.

Best regards,  
Rina Patel  
</body>
